app.notes: A new Bookcase home: books stand on labelled shelves — tap a spine to pull it out. Fifteen new books in the online library: Meditations, Enchiridion, Tao Te Ching, Dhammapada, Arthashastra, The Crowd, As a Man Thinketh, Beyond Good and Evil, The Art of Worldly Wisdom, Maxims, and a new Human Mind shelf with William James, Freud, Darwin, Jung and The Red Book.

books.title: The Art of War
books.author: Sun Tzu
books.blurb: Thirteen short chapters from ancient China on winning — ideally without a fight. Read by generals, CEOs and chess players for 2,500 years.

books.title: The Bhagavad Gita
books.author: Vyasa (trad.)
books.blurb: On a battlefield, a great archer loses his nerve, and his charioteer — God himself — talks him through duty, action, death and devotion. Eighteen chapters of the world's most loved spiritual dialogue.

books.title: The 48 Laws of Power
books.author: Robert Greene
books.blurb: Forty-eight rules of power, from royal courts to modern offices — each law in a minute, paired with a line from Machiavelli, Sun Tzŭ, Gracián or La Rochefoucauld. Know them to use them, or to spot them used on you.

books.title: The Prince
books.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
books.blurb: A banished Florentine diplomat's handbook on how power is won, held and lost. Five hundred years later it still names the game: appearances, fear, loyalty, luck.

books.title: Arthashastra
books.author: Kautilya (Chanakya)
books.blurb: India's ancient handbook of statecraft, by the strategist who helped build the Maurya empire: ministers, spies, money, punishment — and a king who must serve his people.

books.title: Beyond Good and Evil
books.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
books.blurb: Nietzsche's sharpest book: our morals hide deeper drives, every deep thinker wears a mask, and the herd hates whoever stands apart.

books.title: The Crowd
books.author: Gustave Le Bon
books.blurb: A French doctor explains why sensible people turn wild in a mob — the book later studied by propagandists, marketers and dictators.

books.title: The Dhammapada
books.author: The Buddha (trad.)
books.blurb: Short verses from the Buddha's teaching on the mind: what you think, you become.

books.title: Dream Psychology
books.author: Sigmund Freud
books.blurb: Freud's own short guide to his most famous idea: dreams are not nonsense — they are wishes in disguise.

books.title: The Expression of the Emotions
books.author: Charles Darwin
books.blurb: Darwin studies smiles, sneers, tears and blushes in people and animals — the first science of body language.

books.title: The Enchiridion
books.author: Epictetus
books.blurb: A pocket handbook from a philosopher born a slave: separate what you control from what you don't, and you will never be a slave again.

books.title: The Art of Worldly Wisdom
books.author: Baltasar Gracián
books.blurb: Three hundred maxims by a Spanish Jesuit on getting on in a dangerous world — the source behind many of the 48 Laws.

books.title: Talks on Habit
books.author: William James
books.blurb: The father of American psychology on why we are 'walking bundles of habits' — and four rules for building better ones.

books.title: Psychology of the Unconscious
books.author: Carl Gustav Jung
books.blurb: The book that split Jung from Freud: myths, dreams and symbols as the deep, shared language of the human mind.

books.title: Maxims
books.author: François de La Rochefoucauld
books.blurb: A French duke's razor-sharp one-liners about vanity, self-interest and the hidden motives behind our 'virtues'.

books.title: Meditations
books.author: Marcus Aurelius
books.blurb: The private notebook of a Roman emperor, written in army camps at night: how to stay calm, fair and useful when the world is not.

books.title: The Red Book
books.author: Carl Gustav Jung
books.blurb: For sixteen years Jung recorded his own visions in a huge red-leather book, in calligraphy and paintings. Kept secret for a century, it is the map of his journey into the unconscious.

books.title: Tao Te Ching
books.author: Lao Tzu
books.blurb: Eighty-one tiny poems on the Way: soft beats hard, empty is useful, the leader who leads least leads best.

books.title: As a Man Thinketh
books.author: James Allen
books.blurb: A tiny classic of self-help: your thoughts are seeds, your life is the garden.
